CROSS CUT ADHESION TEST KIT CC1000
Product catalog summary
Product Description
The TQC Cross Cut Adhesion Test KIT (CC1000) is designed to assess the adhesion of dry paint coats on substrates through a series of cuts forming a grid pattern. The test involves evaluating the ruled area using a chart after treatment with a brush or adhesive tape for hard substrates.
Business Applications
This product is applicable in sectors such as Protective Coatings, Corrosion Control, Coating Laboratories, and Paint Production.
Standards
The test adheres to standards EN-ISO 2409 and ASTM D3359.
Features
Self-adjusting knife-holder for consistent pressure.
Round cutting knife with eight edges for durability.
Ergonomic handle design.
Easy knife replacement with various sizes available for different standards and substrates.
Scope of Supply
Soft grip handle with CC1000 holder.
Adhesive tape with 4.3N/cm adhesion to steel.
Hardened steel cutter.
4 mm Allen key.
Nylon brush.
Sturdy case.
Illuminated magnifier.
Ordering Information
Various models are available with different blade counts, teeth distances, and coating thickness capabilities, suitable for both ISO and ASTM standards.
Use Instructions
Make perpendicular cuts to form a lattice pattern.
Brush the pattern lightly.
For hard substrates, apply adhesive tape and remove it at specified angles and times according to standards.
Examine and classify the cut area using a magnifier if needed.
Classification
The test results are classified from 0 (5B) to 5 (0B) based on the degree of flaking observed.
Special Care
Clean with a soft, dry cloth.
Avoid mechanical shocks and sharp objects.
Use high-quality alkaline batteries for the magnifier.
Safety Precautions
Handle the knife carefully as it is sharp.

PRODUCT DESCRIPTION The TQC Cross Cut Adhesion Test KIT (CC1000) is used to test the adhesion of dry coats of paint on their substrate by means of a series of cuts through the coating. Two series of parallel cuts cross angled to each other to obtain a pattern of 25 or 100 similar squares. The ruled area is evaluated by using a table chart after a short treatment with a stiff brush, or adhesive tape for hard substrates.
